title: "Visual Encoding and Design"
subtitle: "Phase 3 — From data to interactive product"

## Layer encoding

Three semantic layers are toggled via a navbar tab control. The choice is exclusive: only one layer is active at a time, because each measures a different quantity and has its own colour ramp scale. Showing them simultaneously would invite invalid comparisons.

| Layer | Quantity | Colour ramp | Reasoning |
|:------|:---------|:------------|:----------|
| **Anzahl** | Tier-Anzahl | sequential green | Default view, intuitive ("more livestock = darker"). Green ties into the agricultural domain. |
| **GVE** | Grossvieheinheiten | same green ramp | Apples-to-apples comparison across livestock types. Decouples "intensity" from "raw count". |
| **Futter-Potenzial** | kg Futter / Jahr | same green ramp | Direct business proxy — closely correlates with Verkaufspotenzial in CHF. |

A single sequential ramp across all three layers means the user re-uses one mental colour-to-magnitude mapping. This trades off informational density (you can't compare absolute scales between layers from colour alone) for cognitive simplicity.

## Colour palette

The palette is anchored to two domain colours that read as "agriculture in Thurgau":

| Token | Hex | Role |
|:------|:----|:----|
| `--leaf-d` | `#245220` | dark green (top of choropleth ramp, navbar) |
| `--leaf` | `#3a7a35` | mid green (accents, hover) |
| `--paper2` / `--paper3` | `#e8f0e5` / `#dde8d8` | light green-tinted neutral (ramp start, panel backgrounds) |
| `--wheat` | `#c8900a` | gold accent (Merkliste markers, watchlist highlights) |
| `--brick` | `#a83232` | dark red (destructive: remove, "alle entfernen") |
| `--ink` / `--ink-mid` / `--ink-faint` | `#1a1a1a` / `#555` / `#999` | typographic hierarchy |

The wheat-gold is *only* used for state markers (★ on watchlist items, brief flash on duplicate-add). Reserving it keeps the visual signal-to-noise ratio high.

## Typography

- **Headers and labels**: Lora (serif) — adds editorial gravitas; the dashboard is a decision tool, not a chat app.
- **Body and tabular numerics**: Source Sans 3 with `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` for aligned columns in rankings and the watchlist.

## Layout

The viewport is split horizontally:

- **Left ~70 %**: full-bleed Leaflet choropleth with floating legend (lower-left) and source attribution (lower-right)
- **Right sidebar (~30 %, fixed width)**:
  1. Tierart-Filter chips (Alle, Rinder, Schweine, ...)
  2. Three KPIs (total, top-Gemeinde, average per Gemeinde)
  3. Top-20 ranked list with bars, hover-synced to the map
  4. Merkliste with Excel export
  5. Detail panel (only visible after a click)

This layout puts the map — the *primary* artifact — front and centre, while keeping all interactive controls within thumb reach in the sidebar.

## Interaction model

| Gesture | Effect |
|:--------|:-------|
| Hover ranking row | Highlights corresponding map polygon, shows tooltip |
| Hover map polygon | Highlights ranking row, shows tooltip with top-3 Tierarten |
| Click ranking row or polygon | Opens detail panel with full breakdown + CHF estimate |
| Double-click ranking row or polygon | Adds to Merkliste (+ visual flash if already present) |
| × on Merkliste item | Removes it |
| `↓ Liste als Excel` | Downloads CSV with all 12 attribute columns |
| Layer tabs (Nutztiere / GVE / Futter) | Switches choropleth layer; sidebar values update |
| Tierart chips | Filters values to one livestock category |

`Leaflet.doubleClickZoom` is **disabled** so the double-click gesture can be repurposed for the watchlist without conflicting with map zoom.

## Detail-panel formula

The CHF estimate ("Verkaufspotenzial") is computed inline:

$$
\text{Verkaufspotenzial}_\text{CHF} \;=\; \text{Futter}_\text{kg} \times 0{.}50 \;+\; \text{Einstreu}_\text{kg} \times 0{.}30
$$

The two factors are placeholder unit margins (gemischtes Mineral-/Kraftfutter ≈ 0.50 CHF/kg gross, Stroh/Einstreu ≈ 0.30 CHF/kg). They are explicitly *upper-bound* estimates — the model assumes 100 % of the herd's annual feed/bedding need is purchased through ThurNaturGau. Real numbers would be much smaller and depend on Tierart-specific Zukaufsanteile (ca. 20 % for grazing cattle, 90 %+ for poultry/swine). This refinement is left to a future iteration.

## Rejected alternatives

- **Dot maps** (one dot per animal): would visualize density faithfully, but requires more cognitive effort to compare regions; chosen against because the sidebar already provides ranked numerics.
- **Diverging colour ramp**: appropriate when there's a meaningful midpoint (above/below average). Our quantities are strictly positive and the user wants "where is the most of X", not "where is X above average". Sequential is correct.
- **Multi-layer transparency overlay**: was considered for showing GVE on top of Anzahl. Rejected — comparing transparent overlapping ramps is hard, and the layer toggle is a clearer interaction.
- **Quarto dashboard format** (`format: dashboard`): would have been faster to set up but would lose the custom Leaflet interactions, the watchlist state, and the Excel export. Build-then-deploy as a static HTML keeps full control over the user experience.
